root_cause.text: The driver passed the requested size to dma_free_coherent() instead of the actual aligned allocation size stored in *alloced, causing mismatched DMA memory deallocation when dma_alloc_consistent() returned a larger buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the change from `dma_free_coherent(di->dmadev, size, va, *descpa)` to `dma_free_coherent(di->dmadev, *alloced, va, *descpa)`. The commit message explicitly states that dma_alloc_consistent() "may change the size to align it" and that "the new size is saved in alloced". The bug occurs in the dma_ringalloc function when a reallocation is needed due to alignment constraints.

Allocates memory with the requested size, but the subsequent free does not use the returned actual size, making this line indirectly part of the mismatch vulnerability.
Stores the actual allocated size in '*alloced', which should have been used in the free but was not; thus it is related to the root cause.
Calculates alignment bits from the requested size; while not directly causing the mismatch, it is part of the allocation preparation that leads to the buffer size discrepancy.
Condition that triggers reallocation based on the requested size; if it evaluates true, the vulnerable dma_free_coherent call is executed.
Continuation of the if condition; together with the previous line, it controls when the mismatched free occurs.
